raw_responses.Bulgarian: DESCRIPTION: The figure is a line chart titled "Massive Activation of baseline," plotting "Max Activation Value" on the y-axis against "Layer" on the x-axis. The x-axis ranges from 0 to 22, with labeled tick marks at intervals of 5 (0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 22). The y-axis ranges from 0 to 1600, with labeled tick marks at intervals of 200 (0, 200, 400, 600, 800, 1000, 1200, 1400, 1600). The "attn_output" and "ffn_output" lines remain near zero until layer 5, then spike sharply to around 1400 and 1300 respectively, before dropping back to near zero after layer 15. The "attn_residual" and "ffn_residual" lines remain near zero until layer 5, then rise to approximately 1600 and 1500 respectively, plateauing until layer 20, then sharply decline to around 600 and 500 respectively by layer 22. All lines exhibit a sharp increase at layer 5, followed by a sharp decrease after layer 20.
raw_responses.Chinese:
This line chart, titled "Massive Activation of baseline," displays the maximum activation values across different layers of a neural network model, with four distinct data series plotted against the layer index. The x-axis, labeled "Layer," ranges from 0 to 25 and uses a linear scale with integer tick marks at intervals of 5. The y-axis, labeled "Max Activation Value," ranges from 0 to 1600 and also uses a linear scale with tick marks at intervals of 200. The four lines represent: "attn_output" (blue dashed line), "attn_residual" (orange dotted line), "ffn_output" (green dashed line), and "ffn_residual" (red solid line). The "attn_output" and "attn_residual" lines show a sharp rise starting around layer 5, peaking near 1400, and then declining slightly after layer 20. The "ffn_output" line exhibits a sharp spike to approximately 1100 at layer 5, followed by a steep drop to near zero, with a small secondary peak around layer 14, and then a sharp rise again to about 1200 at layer 22 before falling. The "ffn_residual" line remains near zero until layer 5, then rises sharply to approximately 1500, remains relatively stable until layer 20, and then drops to about 600 before rising again to approximately 1400 at layer 25. All lines are plotted with distinct colors and line styles for clear differentiation.

raw_responses.English: DESCRIPTION: This line plot illustrates the maximum activation values across different layers of a neural network model, specifically comparing four distinct activation pathways: attn_output, attn_residual, ff_n_output, and ff_n_residual. The x-axis represents the layer index, ranging from 0 to 22, with tick marks at regular intervals of 5 units. The y-axis represents the Max Activation Value, scaled linearly from 0 to 1600. The four data series are depicted as follows: attn_output is shown as a blue dashed line that remains near zero until layer 20, then rises to approximately 200; attn_residual is an orange dotted line that peaks near 1600 at layer 5 and remains high until layer 20 before dropping sharply; ff_n_output is a green dashed line that rises sharply to a peak of approximately 1200 at layer 5, then drops to near zero by layer 15 before rising again to approximately 1200 at layer 20; ff_n_residual is a red solid line that mirrors the ff_n_output trend closely, peaking near 1600 at layer 5 and again near 1600 at layer 20, with a dip to approximately 500 at layer 15. All lines are plotted on the same axes with no overlapping or crossing lines beyond their respective peaks and valleys.

Four distinct data series are plotted: 'attn_output' (blue dashed line), 'attn_residual' (orange dotted line), 'ffn_output' (green dashed line), and 'ffn_residual' (red solid line). The 'ffn_output' line remains near zero until layer 10, then spikes to approximately 1000 at layer 12, drops to near zero by layer 15, and rises again to approximately 1200 at layer 22. The 'ffn_residual' line remains near zero until layer 5, then rises to approximately 1400, plateaus until layer 15, and then declines to approximately 600 at layer 22. All lines exhibit sharp increases and decreases at specific layer indices, with no consistent trend across the entire range.
